Overview

OTM is a JSON (or YAML) document format for exchanging one system's threat model between tools. A document has a required otmVersion and project, and lists of assets (with confidentiality, integrity and availability scores), trustZones (nested, each with a trustRating), components (each inside exactly one trust zone or component), dataflows (source to destination), threats (with categories, cwes and likelihood/impact) and mitigations (with riskReduction). A component or data flow holds threat instances, each a reference to a root threat plus a free-string state and its mitigation instances. representations carry diagram layout and code locations. Nine object types carry a free-form attributes map, and no object is closed, so unknown keys validate.

The README marks fields REQUIRED and gives ranges ("From 0 to 100") and reference rules that the schema does not enforce: the schema has no numeric bounds, allows null where the README forbids it, and checks no id uniqueness or reference. distilled/ records both views and a derived strict schema that adds the README's rules.

Applicability

  • Security: core. A security-model format: assets, trust zones, threats, mitigations and their per-component state.
  • Cryptography: none. Defines no cryptographic mechanism.
  • This project: core. ADR-0007 (DEC-002) commits tmodel to importing OTM, with a crosswalk and a round-trip vector. Components, threats, mitigations and cwes map onto ADR-0010's Component, ThreatInstance, Mitigation and Weakness. OTM's assets, trust zones and data flows have no target class in the accepted schema (RPT-0005 gap G13), and OTM has no attack steps, paths, vulnerabilities, products or review records. Details in distilled/design-notes.md.

Artifacts in this record

  • record.yaml — metadata, digests, relations, FX-1 distillation block.
  • distilled/ — the FX-1 artifact set; distilled/README.md indexes each file and its coverage: normative text and requirements from the README and schema, the verbatim schema plus a derived strict schema, every object and field, the instance-state lifecycle, every README example as a fixture with actual validation results, design notes for tmodel, and the verification record.

Limits

  • Pins one commit of one repository. IriusRisk's product documentation, the StartLeft code and any OTM features specific to IriusRisk were not examined.
  • The README and the schema disagree in places; both are extracted and every disagreement is recorded (source_defects in distilled/requirements.yaml). Neither is declared authoritative by the source.
  • The schema text changed in 2024 under the same 0.2.0 id, so "0.2.0" names two different schema texts; this record pins the later one.
  • Vendor-controlled and still 0.x. CONTRIBUTING.md says semver is intended, but "the policy for versioning could change in the future".
  • Gathered for RPT-0003 (tmodel threat-modeling products); fully extracted for RPT-0005 (tmodel #39).
